SOURCE: https://api.osf.io/v2/wikis/tekjq/content/
This experiment aims to replicate and extend the bimodal flanker effect reported in Experiment 2 in Ulrich et al. (2020).

We collected data of N = 147 participants, after preregistered exclusions. In summary, we found significant evidence for bimodal Flanker effects, F(2, 292) = 83.94, p < .001, np2 = .37, and a significant interaction of congruency and flanker modality, F(2, 292) = 4.28, p = .015, np2 = .03.

Ulrich, R., Prislan, L., & Miller, J. (2020). A bimodal extension of the Eriksen flanker task. Attention, Perception, & Psychophysics. https://doi.org/10.3758/s13414-020-02150-8

Hypothesis 1:
decisions.reason: The OSF project reports a completed study (N = 147) aiming to replicate and extend Ulrich, Prislan, & Miller (2020) Experiment 2. As stated in Hypothesis 1 of the linked preregistration, the specific finding of Ulrich et al. (2020) Exp 2 in the auditory flanker condition is that reaction times in the perceptual-congruent condition are significantly faster than in BOTH the response-congruent and incongruent conditions, with no significant difference between the response-congruent and incongruent conditions (indicating purely perceptual rather than response-level cross-modal flanker interference). However, both the OSF wiki summary and the annotated R script (analysis.R) report only the omnibus 3-level congruency main effect in the auditory condition, F(2, 292) = 83.94, p < .001, np2 = .37, and the 2x3 modality-by-congruency interaction, F(2, 292) = 4.28, p = .015, np2 = .03. The script includes code for the planned pairwise paired t-tests and accuracy analyses without any pasted output or cell means. Because a significant 3-level omnibus ANOVA cannot distinguish Ulrich et al.'s specific perceptual-only pattern from a standard response-congruency effect, the replication outcome is undeterminable from the available primary source.
